name: Fellows experimental gear-shaping machine
description: A gear-shaped cutter and synchronized movement were used in a machine designed for generating gear teeth.

impact.note: A more exact and faster way to cut gears, used by gear makers in several countries, with a few later generating machines following it.

date.basis: Date describes the reported event or archaeological context, not the origin of the general technique.

events.statement: The museum dates the first experimental 36-inch-capacity gear shaper to 1896 and says it was never sold.

evidence.supports: The museum dates the first experimental 36-inch-capacity gear shaper to 1896 and says it was never sold.

earliest_record.rationale: First researched event for this local case; it does not establish worldwide priority.

caveats: The museum identifies the first 1896 machine as experimental and unsold; the Smithsonian archival guide describes a 36-inch machine sent to a customer without explicitly resolving this apparent conflict.
